newsitem.title: USA: Olin reaches settlement with U.S. Attorney.
newsitem.headline: Olin reaches settlement with U.S. Attorney.

text.p: Olin Corp said Thursday it had reached an agreement with the U.S. Attorney's Office involving alleged discrepancies in the inspection of 20 mm ammunition produced at one of its facilities.
Under the terms of the settlement reached with the office for the Southern District of Illinois, Olin will pay the Department of Justice $8 million without admitting liability, it said.
The company said the settlement would allow it to finish a feasibility study into spinning off its Ordnance and Aerospace divisions to its shareholders.
It said the settlement followed an investigation by the office into the "in-process" inspection of ammunition at its Ordnance Division facility in Marion, Illinois.
The company said the investigation began after it notified the Department of Defense that one of its employees had disclosed discrepancies in the inspection of the rounds, namely 28/B and M940.
It said the discrepancies did not adversely affect the rounds made for the U.S. Armed Forces and production had resumed.
